header.name: Contract Theory
header.description: This is a standard course in the sequence of Microeconomics courses. The course starts with the classic expected utility model of decision making under uncertainty and the measurement of risk aversion. The focus is on analyzing how informational frictions affect contracts. Principal agent models of hidden action and hidden information are developed. Finally, market equilibria with informational frictions and some standard ways in which markets mitigate these frictions are studied.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to use the expected utility model of decision making under risk.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to analyze how informational asymmetries affect the design of contracts.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to critically examine classic market responses to mitigate informational asymmetries.
